title: David's Census and the Plague
overview: David counts his fighting men, a deadly plague follows as punishment, and it stops when he buys a threshing floor and offers sacrifices there.

parts.label: The order to count (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: The text says the LORD, angry with Israel for reasons it does not give, stirred David to count his soldiers, while the retelling in 1 Chronicles 21 says an adversary, often translated Satan, did the stirring. Even Joab, David's tough army chief, questioned the idea and pushed back.

parts.label: Counting the whole land (vv. 5-9)
parts.note: The officers circled the country, east across the Jordan, north toward Sidon, then down to Beersheba in the far south, taking almost ten months. Their totals differ from those in 1 Chronicles 21, and scholars disagree about how to explain the gap.

parts.label: Guilt and three choices (vv. 10-14)
parts.note: The text never says exactly why counting was wrong, though a common reading is that David was measuring his military strength instead of trusting God, perhaps to draft men for war. Offered years of famine, three months of fleeing from pursuing enemies, or three days of plague, David chose to fall into the LORD's hands, saying his mercy is great, rather than into human hands.

parts.label: The plague is halted (vv. 15-17)
parts.note: Seventy thousand people died, and the text states this plainly without fully explaining why the people suffered for the king's choice. As the angel reached Jerusalem, God called a halt, and David begged that the punishment fall on him and his family instead of on his 'sheep.'

parts.label: David buys the threshing floor (vv. 18-25)
parts.note: Araunah, from Jerusalem's older Jebusite population, offered his threshing floor (a flat open place for beating out grain) for free, but David insisted on paying, saying he would not offer the LORD sacrifices that cost him nothing. 2 Chronicles 3:1 later names this spot as where Solomon built the temple, so the book closes with the plague ending at Israel's future place of worship.

disagreement: Christians differ over how to understand God stirring David to sin and then punishing it, some reading it through Chronicles as God permitting an adversary to act, others as God working through David's own pride.
think: When a leader's choice brings harm on many people, what do you think that leader owes them?
